title: Lunar New Year
strapline: Red lanterns swaying, a dancing dragon winding through the room, and the whole year starting fresh with a wish for good luck.
intent: Lunar New Year, celebrated across many East and Southeast Asian communities, welcomes a fresh year with family, feasting and hopes for good fortune — a bright, energetic festival children take to at once.
Honouring a real celebration from families in the community helps every child value the traditions of their friends and feel seen when their own are shared.
Making lanterns, dragon dancing and creating blossom brings vibrant creative, physical and fine-motor work — cutting, folding, moving, painting.
The traditions carry lovely mathematics — the twelve animals of the zodiac to count and order, red envelopes to fill and match, patterns to repeat.
Children grow real knowledge of the wider world and new vocabulary — lantern, dragon, blossom, celebrate, lucky, feast, family.
Dragon dancing together, sharing food and giving good wishes builds cooperation, movement and joyful belonging.
implementation: Learn about the festival with families who celebrate it — invite them to share their traditions and foods, and follow their lead so it stays accurate and respectful.
Offer lantern-making, red-envelope crafts, blossom painting and a long fabric dragon for children to dance beneath together.
Model the language and wonder: 'This is the Year of the animal — I wonder which animals came before it. Shall we line them up?'
Bring in maths through the traditions — order the zodiac animals, count coins into red envelopes, repeat patterns on lanterns.
Move and celebrate together — dragon and lion dancing, drums and instruments, so the physical joy of the festival is real.
Share special foods where you safely can (checking allergies, with families), and make good-luck cards and wishes to give.
key_questions: This is the Year of the animal — which animals came before it? Shall we line them up?
How many coins shall we put in each red envelope?
What pattern is on your lantern?
How does the dragon move when we all work together?
How does your family celebrate the new year at home?

impact.text: Children value a real festival from their friends' families and feel seen when their own is shared.
Children make lanterns, dance the dragon and paint blossom — cutting, folding, moving, painting.
Children count and order the twelve zodiac animals and fill and match red envelopes.
Children grow words for the festival — lantern, dragon, blossom, celebrate, lucky, feast.
Children dance the dragon together, building cooperation, movement and joyful belonging.

enhancements: A long fabric dragon for children to dance beneath together.
Lantern-making, red-envelope crafts and blossom painting.
The zodiac animals to order and count.
Drums and instruments for dragon and lion dancing.
Special foods shared where safe, and good-luck cards to make and give.

playing_exploring: Children throw themselves into the movement, colour and sound of a joyful festival, bringing their own family traditions to it.
They make, paint, fold and dance their way into the celebration.
active_learning: Children cooperate to dance the dragon and see through the making of lanterns and cards, absorbed in the shared event.
creating_thinking: Children order the zodiac animals and repeat lantern patterns, and make sense of a celebration alongside their own.
